exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Equation of a Level Surface

question.text: For the function $f(x,y,z) = x^2+y^2+z^2,$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=9.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = 9.$ So, we have:

\begin{align} f(x,y,z) &= c \\[3pt] x^2+y^2+z^2&=9 \end{align}

Therefore, the level surface for $c=9$ is the sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2=9.$

question.text: For the function $f(x,y,z) = e^z - x^2 - y^2,$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z) = 4.$
question.explanation:
The level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = 4.$ So, we have \begin{align} f(x,y,z) & = c \\[3pt] e^z - x^2 - y^2 & = 4\\[3pt] e^{z} & = x^2 + y^2 + 4\\[3pt] z & = \ln(x^2 + y^2 + 4). \end{align}

Therefore, the level surface for $c = 4$ is the surface $z = \ln(x^2 + y^2 + 4).$

question.text: For the function $f(x,y,z) = \dfrac{z-\ln(x+y)}{e^{x-y}},$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z) = -2.$
question.explanation:
The level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = -2.$ So, we have:

\begin{align} f(x,y,z) &= c \\[3pt] \dfrac{z-\ln(x+y)}{e^{x-y}}&=-2\\[3pt] z-\ln(x+y) &= -2e^{x-y} \\[3pt] z &= \ln(x+y)-2e^{x-y} \end{align}

Therefore, the level surface for $c=-2$ is the surface $z = \ln(x+y)-2e^{x-y}.$

question.text: For the function $f(x,y,z) = e^{x^2 + y^2 - z - 1},$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z) = 1.$
question.explanation:
The level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = 1.$ So, we have \begin{align} f(x,y,z) & = c \\[3pt] e^{x^2 + y^2 - z - 1} & = 1\\[3pt] x^2 + y^2 - z - 1 & = 0\\[3pt] z & = x^2 + y^2 - 1. \end{align}

Therefore, the level surface for $c = 1$ is the paraboloid $z = x^2 + y^2 - 1.$

question.text: For the function $f(x,y,z) = 12z^2-3x^2-2y^2,$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=12.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = 12.$ So, we have:

\begin{align} f(x,y,z) &= c \\[3pt] 12z^2-3x^2-2y^2&=12 \\[5pt] \dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac{y^2}{6} - z^2 &= -1 \end{align}

Therefore, the level surface for $c=12$ is the hyperboloid of two sheets $\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac{y^2}{6}-z^2=-1.$

question.text: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z) = x^2 + y^2 - \ln z?$
question.choice1: A family of curves: $z  = e^{x^2 + y^2 - c}$
question.choice4: A family of hyperbolic paraboloids: $z = x^2 - y^2 + c$
question.choice5: A family of paraboloids: $z = x^2 + y^2 + c$
question.explanation:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation: \begin{align*} f(x,y,z) &= c \\[3pt] x^2 + y^2 - \ln z & = c \\[3pt] \ln z & = x^2 + y^2 - c \\[3pt] z & =e^{x^2 + y^2 - c} \end{align*}

Therefore, we get a family of curves: \[ z = e^{x^2 + y^2 - c}, \quad c \in(-\infty, \infty) \]

question.text: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z) = -x^2 - 3y^2 + z + 3?$
question.choice1: A family of elliptic paraboloids: $z = x^2 + 3y^2 + C$
question.choice2: A family of hyperbolic paraboloids: $z = x^2 - 3y^2 + C$
question.choice3: A family of elliptic cones: $z^2 = x^2 + 3y^2 + C$
question.choice4: A family of planes: $z = x + 3y + C$
question.choice5: A family of elliptic paraboloids: $z = -x^2 - 3y^2 + C$
question.explanation:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation: \begin{align*} f(x,y,z) &= c \\[3pt] -x^2 - 3y^2 + z + 3 & = c \\[3pt] z &= x^2 + 3y^2 + c - 3 \end{align*}

If we let $c - 3 =C,$ we get a family of elliptic paraboloids: \[ z = x^2 + 3y^2 + C, \quad C\in(-\infty,\infty) \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Level Surface of a Function Passing Through a Point

question.text: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z) = \ln(xyz)-\sqrt{xy}$ that passes through the point $P(1,1,e).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

\begin{align*} f(1,1,e) &= \ln(1\cdot 1\cdot e)-\sqrt{1\cdot 1} = 0 \end{align*}

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = 0.$ So, we have:

\begin{align*} f(x,y,z) &= c \\[3pt] \ln(xyz)-\sqrt{xy} &= 0 \\[5pt] \ln(xyz) &= \sqrt{xy} \\[5pt] xyz &= e^{\sqrt{xy}} \\[5pt] z &= \dfrac{e^{\sqrt{xy}}}{xy} \end{align*}

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(1,1,e)$ is the surface $z = \dfrac{e^{\sqrt{xy}}}{xy}.$

question.text: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z) = x - 2y + z$ that passes through the point $P(1, 1, -1).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the value of the function at $P{:}$ \begin{align*} f(1,1,-1) & = 1 - 2(1) + (-1)\\[3pt] & = 1 - 2 - 1\\[3pt] & = -2 \end{align*}

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = -2.$ So, we have \begin{align*} f(x,y,z) & = c \\[3pt] x - 2y + z & = -2\\[3pt] x - 2y + z + 2 & = 0. \end{align*}

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(1,1,-1)$ is the plane $x - 2y + z + 2 = 0.$

question.text: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z) = z-4x^2-6y^2$ that passes through the point $P(2,1,22).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

\begin{align*} f(2,1,22) &= 22-4(2)^2-6(1)^2 = 0 \end{align*}

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = 0.$ So, we have:

\begin{align*} f(x,y,z) &= c \\[3pt] z-4x^2-6y^2 &= 0 \\[5pt] z&= 4x^2+6y^2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(2,1,22)$ is the elliptic paraboloid $z = 4x^2 + 6y^2.$

question.text: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z) = \dfrac{z}{y-x}$ that passes through the point $P(2, 1, 3).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the value of the function at $P{:}$ \begin{align*} f(2,1,3) & = \dfrac{z}{y-x}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3}{1 - 2}\\[5pt] & = -3 \end{align*}

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = -3.$ So, we have \begin{align*} f(x,y,z) & = c \\[3pt] \dfrac{z}{y - x} & = -3\\[3pt] z & = -3(y - x)\\[3pt] z & = 3x - 3y\\[3pt] 3x - 3y - z & = 0. \end{align*}

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(2,1,3)$ is the plane $3x - 3y - z = 0.$

question.text: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z) = e^{x-y+z-1}$ that passes through the point $P(1, 1, 1).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the value of the function at $P{:}$ \begin{align*} f(1,1,1) & = e^{1 - 1 + 1 - 1}\\[3pt] & = e^{0}\\[5pt] & = 1 \end{align*}

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation \[ f(x,y,z) = c. \]

In our case, we're interested in $c = 1.$ So, we have \begin{align*} f(x,y,z) & = c \\[3pt] e^{x-y+z-1} & = 1\\[3pt] x - y + z - 1 & = 0. \end{align*}

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(1,1,1)$ is the plane $x - y + z - 1 = 0.$
